ops.name: anim.bake_follow
ops.summary: Make a follower animation (a MetaHuman face's) carry its leader's pose: bake_pose from the leader (the body) into `out` for every non-facial bone the two skeletons share, and switch the face rig's own head control off (headcontrolswitch 0)
ops.doc:
Make a follower animation (a MetaHuman face's) carry its leader's pose: bake_pose from the leader (the body)
into `out` for every non-facial bone the two skeletons share, and switch the face rig's own head control off
(headcontrolswitch 0) unless `head_control`, so the head turns only as the body's does. A face playing alone
otherwise keeps its neck and chest apart from the body, and its chest pokes through the clothes. Multi-tick.

ops.name: anim.bake_pose
ops.summary: Sample `source` (a skeletal mesh component of the actor) as it really plays in `sequence` (animation, rig and post-process correctives included) and write those bones, local to their parents, as bone tracks into `out` (a copy of `anim`), wh
ops.doc:
Sample `source` (a skeletal mesh component of the actor) as it really plays in `sequence` (animation, rig and
post-process correctives included) and write those bones, local to their parents, as bone tracks into `out` (a
copy of `anim`), which then goes on `target`'s track. Keys past the sequence keep the animation's own pose; curves
are untouched. A multi-tick job.

ops.name: anim.gaze_lock
ops.summary: Keep a talking face's eyes on the lens, measured rather than guessed: `out` (a copy of `anim`) goes on `component`'s track in `sequence` (on the sections that play `anim`, wherever they start); the eye-look curves are calibrated on the rig,
ops.doc:
Keep a talking face's eyes on the lens, measured rather than guessed: `out` (a copy of `anim`) goes on
`component`'s track in `sequence` (on the sections that play `anim`, wherever they start); the eye-look curves are
calibrated on the rig, then solved per frame from the eye bones' real pose (head and body motion included)
toward `camera`, with small saccades, and refined `iterations` times against a fresh measurement.
`target` aims the eyes elsewhere: a point [x, y, z], an actor (+ `target_offset` in its frame) or
"Label:Component:bone" (her eyes: "Presenter:Face:FACIAL_L_Eye"); with `frames` [first, last] only in that range
(the camera, if given, elsewhere). Frames with neither keep the animation's own eye curves. Returns the angle error
per pass. A multi-tick job.

ops.name: anim.head_to_body
ops.summary: Give the body the head motion a face rig makes from speech (HeadYaw/Pitch/Roll spread down the neck): bake the face's spine, neck and head as they play into `out` (a copy of the body's animation), which goes on the body's track.
ops.doc:
Give the body the head motion a face rig makes from speech (HeadYaw/Pitch/Roll spread down the neck): bake the
face's spine, neck and head as they play into `out` (a copy of the body's animation), which goes on the body's
track. Then bake_follow puts the whole shared skeleton back on the face, so both move as one. Multi-tick.

ops.summary: A material instance: kind Surface (color, roughness, metallic, specular), Textured (a texture tinted by color, tiled), Screen (an emitted texture x intensity behind glossy glass), Emissive (color x intensity, unlit), Glass (translucent, opa
ops.doc:
A material instance: kind Surface (color, roughness, metallic, specular), Textured (a texture tinted by color,
tiled), Screen (an emitted texture x intensity behind glossy glass), Emissive (color x intensity, unlit), Glass
(translucent, opacity), ScreenBlink (Screen with a baked-in cursor that blinks: scalars Blink 0-1 and the cursor's
UV rectangle CursorU0, CursorU1, CursorV0, CursorV1), Pbr (texture, normal and mask maps; mask R x roughness,
G x metallic), PbrMasked (Pbr cut out by the texture's alpha), Sheer (backlit thin fabric: mask B x opacity,
dithered; transmission colour, glow), Glow (texture x color x intensity, additive) or GlowWipe (Glow revealed
left to right: scalars Reveal 0-1 and Softness; it also takes the lower of Reveal and MPC_FM's WipeReveal, and is
multiplied by MPC_FM's WipeOn, both 1 unless a sequence keys them). `scalars` sets any other scalar parameters by

ops.doc:

ops.name: mh.cloth_inflate
ops.summary: Push a garment out along its normals by `cm`, so skin under tight cloth stops poking through.
ops.doc:
Push a garment out along its normals by `cm`, so skin under tight cloth stops poking through. A multi-tick job.

Nothing the renderer is drawing is ever edited: a material in use that is reparented or recompiled while frames
render trips `UniformExpressionCache... == Material.GetRenderingThreadShaderMap()` and takes the editor down (it
did, right after a MetaHuman rebuild had made fresh garment instances). So the worn instance is copied to
`{folder}/{label}_<name>_Inflate`, the copy is parented on project copies of its plugin chain whose master gains a
World Position Offset (normal x FM_Inflate), every shader finishes compiling, the editor ticks a few frames, and
only then does the component swap to the copy. A master already in use is never recompiled (a new one is made);
re-running on an inflated garment only changes the amount, a plain parameter change that is safe. `which` limits it
to the garments whose material name contains it (e.g. "Shirt": a top pushed out over shorts that stay put, else
both move together and the shorts' waistband still shows through the tee); others already inflated go back to 0.

ops.name: render.mrq
ops.summary: Start a Movie Render Queue job (returns at once; poll render.progress).
ops.doc:
Start a Movie Render Queue job (returns at once; poll render.progress). Frames go to `out_dir` as
{frame}.png|exr|jpg, the audio as a wav; `start`/`end` (end exclusive) render part of the sequence. `executor`:
"pie" (in this editor) or "process" (a separate -game process; offscreen where the editor has no desktop). The
process loads the level from disk, and with unsaved changes the executor asks to save first: unattended, that
question goes unanswered and the job never starts, so unsaved packages are an error unless `save_dirty`.

ops.name: seq.anim
ops.summary: Animation sections on an actor's skeletal mesh component (a MetaHuman's "Body" or "Face"), each {"anim", "start", "end", "offset", "blend_in", "blend_out", "rate", "weight", "loop", "row"}: `start`/`end` frames (end default: start + the ani
ops.doc:
Animation sections on an actor's skeletal mesh component (a MetaHuman's "Body" or "Face"), each
{"anim", "start", "end", "offset", "blend_in", "blend_out", "rate", "weight", "loop", "row"}: `start`/`end`
frames (end default: start + the animation's length / rate; past that it loops, `loop` False holds the last
pose), `offset` seconds into the animation where it starts, `blend_in`/`blend_out` frames of ease (weights
cross-fade where sections overlap: idle -> line -> idle), `weight` (1), `row` (default: the first free one; overlaps
go on separate rows). `replace` clears the track's sections first, else these are added. Returns [[anim, start,
end, row]].

ops.name: seq.audio
ops.summary: Sounds in a sequence on a named audio track ("VO", "Score", "SFX"): clips [{"sound", "start", "end", "offset", "volume"}] or [sound, start]: a SoundWave asset (assets.import a WAV first) from frame `start`, `offset` seconds into it, to `end
ops.doc:
Sounds in a sequence on a named audio track ("VO", "Score", "SFX"): clips [{"sound", "start", "end", "offset",
"volume"}] or [sound, start]: a SoundWave asset (assets.import a WAV first) from frame `start`, `offset` seconds
into it, to `end` (default: its length), at `volume` (1). For timing in the editor; the mix is made in post.
`replace` empties the named track first, else adds to it. Returns [[sound, start, end, row]].

ops.name: seq.key_collection
ops.summary: Key a scalar parameter of a material parameter collection (look.collection) on the sequence's track for that collection: keys [[frame, value(, interp)], ...].
ops.doc:
Key a scalar parameter of a material parameter collection (look.collection) on the sequence's track for that
collection: keys [[frame, value(, interp)], ...]. Sequencer writes the world's instance of the collection, so the
value reaches every material reading it with no mesh binding and no MID in between. Replaces only that
parameter's keys.

ops.name: seq.key_color
ops.summary: Key a colour property: keys [[frame, [r, g, b(, a)](, interp)], ...].
ops.doc:
Key a colour property: keys [[frame, [r, g, b(, a)](, interp)], ...]. An FColor property (a light's
"LightColor") takes sRGB 0-1, as look.light does; an FLinearColor one (fog "FogInscatteringLuminance", a post
"Settings.ColorGain") takes linear values. `srgb` overrides that guess. Component and replacement as key_float.

ops.name: seq.key_float
ops.summary: Key a float property of an actor or component: keys [[frame, value(, interp)], ...], interp "auto" (smooth, eased at held ends), "linear" or "constant" (stepped).
ops.doc:
Key a float property of an actor or component: keys [[frame, value(, interp)], ...], interp "auto" (smooth,
eased at held ends), "linear" or "constant" (stepped). `prop` is the C++ name or a path into structs, either
spelling: "Intensity", "Temperature", "FocusSettings.ManualFocusDistance" (CameraComponent), "CurrentAperture",
"Settings.AutoExposureBias" (a PostProcessVolume actor: set its override flag once with look.post), "FogDensity".
`component` by name or class ("CameraComponent", "LightComponent0"); "" = the actor if it has the property, else
its root component (a light's). `double` for a double property (a UE5 large-world value). Replaces only this
property's track on that binding; the keys hold before the first and after the last.

ops.name: seq.key_material
ops.summary: Key a material parameter on a mesh component's material slot (the material there must be an instance or material with that parameter): keys [[frame, value(, interp)], ...], a float for a scalar parameter or [r, g, b(, a)] (linear) for a vec
ops.doc:
Key a material parameter on a mesh component's material slot (the material there must be an instance or
material with that parameter): keys [[frame, value(, interp)], ...], a float for a scalar parameter or
[r, g, b(, a)] (linear) for a vector one. `slot` is its index or name ("M_Sheer"); `component` "" = the actor's
first mesh component. Replaces only that parameter's keys in the slot's track; other parameters keep theirs.

ops.name: seq.key_transform
ops.summary: Animate an actor in a sequence: keys are [frame, [x, y, z], {"pitch", "yaw", "roll"} | [x, y, z] to look at] with an optional 4th element, the interpolation leaving that key: "auto" (smooth, eases at held ends), "linear" or "constant" (hold
ops.doc:
Animate an actor in a sequence: keys are [frame, [x, y, z], {"pitch", "yaw", "roll"} | [x, y, z] to look at]
with an optional 4th element, the interpolation leaving that key: "auto" (smooth, eases at held ends), "linear"
or "constant" (hold until the next key, a jump cut). `interp` is the default. Replaces the actor's transform
track (and only that), keeping the actor's scale; yaw is keyed as given, so unwrap it yourself across +-180.

ops.name: seq.key_visible
ops.summary: Show and hide an actor (or one of its components) over a sequence: keys [[frame, visible], ...], stepped; the first key holds before it.
ops.doc:
Show and hide an actor (or one of its components) over a sequence: keys [[frame, visible], ...], stepped; the
first key holds before it. Overrides the level's hidden state while the sequence is open or playing (a
presenter hidden in the level can appear in the reel). `attached` keys the actors attached to it too (her
earrings and watch). Replaces only the visibility track.

ops.name: seq.new
ops.summary: An empty level sequence for building into (no actor, no camera): playback [start, end) at `fps`.
ops.doc:
An empty level sequence for building into (no actor, no camera): playback [start, end) at `fps`. If it exists it
is kept as it is (only its range set), so several scripts can each add their tracks; `replace` starts it afresh.

ops.name: seq.rebind
ops.summary: Point a sequence's actor bindings at the level's actors of the same label again, after the level was rebuilt and the old actors are gone (their tracks are kept; a binding removed and remade would lose them).
ops.doc:
Point a sequence's actor bindings at the level's actors of the same label again, after the level was rebuilt
and the old actors are gone (their tracks are kept; a binding removed and remade would lose them). `labels` None
= every actor binding whose name is an actor in the level. Returns {label: "ok" | "missing"}.

ops.name: seq.sample
ops.summary: Play a sequence frame by frame across editor ticks (so animation and rigs settle) and record bones' world transforms, each [x, y, z, axis_x(3), axis_y(3), axis_z(3)], `camera`'s location, and `target`'s (see seq.aim_point: a point, an actor
ops.doc:
Play a sequence frame by frame across editor ticks (so animation and rigs settle) and record bones' world
transforms, each [x, y, z, axis_x(3), axis_y(3), axis_z(3)], `camera`'s location, and `target`'s (see
seq.aim_point: a point, an actor, "Label:Component:bone"). A multi-tick job.

ops.summary: Open a sequence in Sequencer, locked to its camera, at a frame (for checking a pose in the viewport).

ops.name: seq.set_anim

ops.doc:
Swap the animation on a component's track in a sequence: every section of it, or only those playing `only`.
`label` picks the actor when several have a component of that name (both presenters have "Body").

ops.name: seq.shot
ops.summary: A shot: `anims` maps component names to animations ({"Body": idle, "Face": talk}); `audio` a SoundWave; the camera cut on `camera`.
ops.doc:
A shot: `anims` maps component names to animations ({"Body": idle, "Face": talk}); `audio` a SoundWave; the
camera cut on `camera`. Length: `seconds`, else the audio's, else the longest animation's.

ops.name: seq.still
ops.summary: A still of a sequence at a frame through `camera`, or, with camera "", through the camera the edit (the camera cut track) shows at that frame: scrub there, let it settle `settle` ticks (temporal anti-aliasing, Lumen), capture.
ops.doc:
A still of a sequence at a frame through `camera`, or, with camera "", through the camera the edit (the camera
cut track) shows at that frame: scrub there, let it settle `settle` ticks (temporal anti-aliasing, Lumen),
capture. A multi-tick job.

ops.name: seq.stills
ops.summary: Stills of a sequence at many frames ({out_dir}/{frame:04d}.png): a contact sheet's worth in one call.
ops.doc:
Stills of a sequence at many frames ({out_dir}/{frame:04d}.png): a contact sheet's worth in one call. Through
one `camera`, or with camera "" each frame through its own shot's camera (the camera cut track): a previs of the
whole cut. A multi-tick job; returns [[frame, camera, path]].

ops.name: seq.tracks
ops.summary: What a sequence holds: for each binding (an actor, or actor.component) its tracks as [class, property or name, sections, keys]; master tracks under "".
ops.doc:
What a sequence holds: for each binding (an actor, or actor.component) its tracks as [class, property or
name, sections, keys]; master tracks under "". For checking what a build script made.

ops.doc: The audio solver's moods (AUTO_DETECT, CONFIDENCE, EXCITEMENT, HAPPINESS, ...).

ops.name: speech.to_face
ops.summary: Import `wav` (a path on the workstation), solve it with MetaHuman Animator's audio solver in `mood` at `intensity`, and export an animation on `face_mesh`'s skeleton.
ops.doc:
Import `wav` (a path on the workstation), solve it with MetaHuman Animator's audio solver in `mood` at
`intensity`, and export an animation on `face_mesh`'s skeleton. Returns the sound, performance and animation.
A multi-tick job.

areas.anim: Animation curves: read and write a sequence's float curves, and lock a talking face's gaze on the camera.
areas.assets: Assets: list, import, duplicate, delete, save.
areas.level: Levels and actors: new/open/save, list, spawn (shapes, assets, classes), move, aim, delete.
areas.look: The look: materials (surface, emissive, glass), lights (rect, spot, point), atmosphere (volumetric fog), post-process and cine cameras, plus quick stills through a camera for checking a frame without a render.
areas.mh: MetaHumans: presets, a character from a preset, Epic's cloud rig and high-resolution textures, wardrobe (hair, beard, brows, clothes), the cinematic build to a Blueprint, and how an assembled character is driven.
areas.ops: The bridge's operations: named functions the operator's machine calls through POST /op (fmbridge.server), each a plain Python function over the `unreal` API, registered with @op("area.verb").
areas.render: Renders with Movie Render Queue: image sequences plus the mixed audio, deferred (Lumen) or path-traced, with temporal/spatial samples and console variables for quality.
areas.seq: Level sequences: a shot from an actor, animations per component, audio and a camera; open and scrub.
areas.speech: Speech to face: a voice file on the workstation becomes a MetaHuman facial animation (lip-sync, blinks, brows, head movement), through MetaHuman Animator's audio solver with a chosen mood.
